source_title: Brentford capitalise as Nottingham Forest’s attacking struggles continue
source_excerpt:
For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest , the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”.
“For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation that the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.”
Forest, once again, didn’t play too badly. No side has underperformed their xG as significantly as Forest, who went into the weekend third in Opta’s expected table but third-bottom in real life. Here, they had two-and-a-half times as many chances as Brentford . They could claim a degree of misfortune in that both goals went in off the luckless Nikola Milenkovic, the first an own goal after Murillo had misjudged a long clearance to Dango Ouattara, the second credited to Igor Thiago as he latched on to Jaydon Anthony’s clever low cross. But Glasner was accepting no excuses. “It’s not anger,” he said. “It’s necessary.”
The result, Glasner said, was “disappointing and frustrating. And we have to accept it’s not good enough. If you lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why it’s for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.”
One player, he revealed, had asked to travel home alone. “I said no, we can go back with the coach. For example, I have no understanding if somebody wants to go home on his own today from London to Nottingham. No, go with the bus like everybody else. No extras, no extras.”
What the change looks like remains to be seen. Glasner was keen to stress that he takes full responsibility and, at times, seemed to have sympathy. “They tried,” he said. “You can’t say they’ve had a lack of effort. But again, you feel you’re controlling the game. You create a few good situations, and all of a sudden you’re 1-0 down. It was the fourth goal we conceded from a long ball from a goalkeeper. So it’s lack of awareness, losing then the duel, and we’re 1-0 down.
“It’s not a lack of effort, but there are a few things that are very obvious. We’re talking about the realities. We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it. And if you can’t change it, we need different personnel. And if the club doesn’t want to change it, they need a different manager. I’m desperate to change it. Desperate.
“I think we see the football is OK. We don’t give them many chances. So we kept them to seven [Opta stats said six] shots here at Brentford. So we are creating enough situations. We have the personnel. But we need to get more out of the players. And this is where I see my responsibility. I felt it was more hugging than now. But if hugging doesn’t work, there’s also an opposite way. And again, I don’t need to be liked. I’m not here to be liked. I’m here to bring success to this club. And that’s what I think. Not what I think. That’s what I will change.”
• Brentford have scored the opening goal in eight of their last nine Premier League games, and only Manchester City (37) and Arsenal (32) have done so more often in the competition since the start of last season than the Bees (27).
• Nottingham Forest have failed to score in five of their nine Premier League games this season, no side has done so more; that’s despite having more xG than their opponents in seven of those nine matches.
• Since the start of last season, only Erling Haaland (33), João Pedro (20) and Antoine Semenyo (18) have scored more non-penalty goals in the Premier League than the 16 of Igor Thiago (pictured). Opta
For his part, Keith Andrews described the win, bafflingly Brentford’s first since they beat Chelsea before the last international break, as their best of the season. “We had to show different traits to some of the other games,” he said. “There was a lot of smart play and leadership from our players.”
Unless morale disintegrates completely, Forest, surely, will be fine. The ball will start running for them. But for now the fates remain against them. And it is that, more than anything, that Glasner needs to change.

## परिचय
ब्रेंटफोर्ड के खिलाफ एक और निराशाजनक हार के बाद नॉटिंघम फॉरेस्ट के मैनेजर ओलिवर ग्लासनर ने टीम में बड़े बदलावों के संकेत दिए हैं। मैच के बाद उनकी प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस काफी तनावपूर्ण रही, जिसमें उन्होंने टीम के प्रदर्शन और अपनी रणनीतियों पर खुलकर बात की।

## मैच का घटनाक्रम और परिणाम
ब्रेंटफोर्ड के खिलाफ मुकाबले में फॉरेस्ट की टीम ने अधिक मौके बनाए, लेकिन भाग्य ने उनका साथ नहीं दिया।
- निकोला मिलेंकोविच के आत्मघाती गोल और इगोर थियागो के गोल के चलते टीम को हार का सामना करना पड़ा।
- आंकड़ों के अनुसार, फॉरेस्ट ने मैच में अधिक अवसर सृजित किए, लेकिन परिणाम उनके पक्ष में नहीं रहा।
- पिछले पांच मैचों में यह टीम की चौथी हार है, जिससे स्थिति और गंभीर हो गई है।

## मैनेजर ओलिवर ग्लासनर की प्रतिक्रिया
मैच के बाद 14 मिनट तक चली प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस में ग्लासनर बेहद गुस्से और निराशा में नजर आए। उन्होंने डेस्क पर हाथ पीटते हुए स्वीकार किया कि उन्होंने अपने सिद्धांतों से समझौता किया है। 

ग्लासनर ने स्पष्ट शब्दों में कहा कि जो खिलाड़ी टीम के साथ पूरी तरह से नहीं जुड़ेंगे, वे क्लब छोड़ सकते हैं। उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि एक खिलाड़ी ने अकेले घर लौटने की अनुमति मांगी थी, जिसे उन्होंने खारिज कर दिया और पूरी टीम के साथ बस से लौटने का निर्देश दिया।

## आगे की चुनौतियां और सुधार
क्लब के सामने इस समय मैदान के भीतर और बाहर दोनों मोर्चों पर सुधार की चुनौती है।
- ग्लासनर ने कहा कि वह बिना किसी समझौते के निचले स्तर से पुनर्निर्माण शुरू करेंगे।
- टीम के पास मौकों की कमी नहीं है, लेकिन गोल करने और मौकों को भुनाने में निरंतर विफलता मिल रही है।
- आने वाले हफ्तों में यह देखना होगा कि प्रबंधन और खिलाड़ी इन सख्त बदलावों पर कैसे प्रतिक्रिया देते हैं।

## सत्यापन और मूल जानकारी
इस रिपोर्ट में दिए गए दावे और बयान मैच के बाद आयोजित प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस और उपलब्ध खेल आंकड़ों पर आधारित हैं। पाठक मूल घोषणाओं और आधिकारिक बयानों के लिए क्लब की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट या संबंधित प्रीमियर लीग मैच रिपोर्ट देख सकते हैं।

## Manager Signals Major Overhaul Following Latest Loss

Following a defeat against Brentford, Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner delivered a frank assessment of his team's trajectory, addressing underlying issues after a match decided by decisive moments rather than a lack of overall effort. 

According to reported post-match remarks, Glasner accepted full responsibility for the result while signaling that sweeping changes are imminent. The manager emphasized that a complete internal rebuild is required to address ongoing struggles.

## Key Match and Statistical Dynamics

* **Goal Sequence:** Brentford secured victory via two goals deflected off Nikola Milenkovic, including an opening own goal following a defensive misjudgment and a second credited to Igor Thiago.
* **Underlying Numbers:** Statistics indicate Forest created significantly more chances than their opponents during the fixture, maintaining a pattern where the side frequently outperforms opponents in expected goals metrics without securing corresponding results.
* **Broader Trends:** Reports note that Forest have failed to score in five of their nine Premier League fixtures this season, highlighting a persistent difficulty in converting attacking situations into actual goals.

## Practical Implications and Accountability

Glasner stressed that stricter standards will be enforced moving forward, rejecting individual exceptions such as requests to travel independently from London back to Nottingham. He stated that players must fully commit to his principles or risk departing the club.

While external analysts suggest that statistical indicators point toward future improvement if performance levels are maintained, the manager insisted that a cultural and structural reset is immediately necessary. Verification of these developments and official club updates can be found through official Premier League channels and club media announcements.
en_title: Oliver Glasner Demands Radical Reset After Nottingham Forest's Defeat at Brentford
